nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-01.prompt: Compute the number of possible ways to place 6 identical stones on a $6\times 6$ chessboard so that no two lie in the same row or same column.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-02.prompt: Regular pentagon $ABCDE$ has sides of length 3. Let $R$ be the region composed of points outside $ABCDE$ which are at a distance of at most 1 from some point of $ABCDE$. Compute the area of $R$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-04.prompt: Euler drove from Basel to St. Petersburg. For half the distance of his trip he traveled at 60 miles per hour (mph). For half the time of his trip he traveled at 40 mph. For the remaining portion of his trip he traveled at 50 mph. Compute his average speed for the whole trip, in mph.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-05.prompt: A non-constant geometric progression of real numbers has the property that its $1^{\text{st}}$, $3^{\text{rd}}$ and $5^{\text{th}}$ terms form an arithmetic progression. Compute the common ratio of the geometric progression.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-06.prompt: Non-degenerate triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(-1,0)$, $B(1,0)$ and $C(s,t)$ and the lines $x=1$ and $y=2$ each divide the triangle into two regions of equal area. Compute the ordered pair $(s, t)$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-07.prompt: If $\cos t=\frac{2}{\sqrt5}\ (0^\circ<t<90^\circ)$, compute the value of $(\log_5\cos t)+(\log_5\tan t)$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-08.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$ with right angle $A$ as in the diagram below, $AB=4$ and $AC=3$. Circle $O$ is inscribed in $\triangle ABC$. $\overline{AC}$ is extended to point $D$ such that circle $P$ is inscribed in $\triangle BCD$. If both circles have the same radius, compute $CD$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-09.prompt: Two right circular cones of height 12 and base radius 4 are situated in space so that the vertex of each is the center of the base of the other. Compute the volume of their intersection.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-10.prompt: If $f(0)=3$ and for each integer $n\ge0$, $f(n+1)=3\cdot f(0)\cdot f(1)\cdot f(2)\cdot\cdots\cdot f(n)$, then $f(10)=p^a$, for some prime $p$ and integer $a$, compute $(p, a)$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-11.prompt: If $x=\sqrt{2+\sqrt{6+\sqrt{2+\sqrt{6+\cdots}}}}$ is a root of $x^4+hx^2+ax+m=0$, compute the ordered triple $(h, a, m)$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-12.prompt: A jar holds $g$ green and 17 blue marbles, for integer $g$. Pascal reaches into the jar and selects three marbles at random, without replacement. Compute all three possible values of $g$ so that the probability that Pascal chooses three green marbles is the same as the probability that Pascal chooses two green and one blue marble.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-13.prompt: Compute $n$ such that a regular $n$-gon has twice as many diagonals as sides.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-14.prompt: There are four given numbers, $w$, $x$, $y$ and $z$, and there are six pairwise sums which can be formed, $w+x, w+y, w+z, x+y, x+z$ and $y+z$. For some choice of $w$, $x$, $y$ and $z$, five of these sums are 13, 25, 36, 39 and 48. Compute the sixth sum.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-15.prompt: Let $R$ be the portion of the interior of unit square $ABCD$ composed of all points $X$ such that: $AX<BX<DX<CX$. Compute the area of $R$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-16.prompt: A positive integer $n$ is called a *$b$-$d$-palindrome* if its representation in base $b$ is the same as its representation in base $d$ except with the digits reversed (no leading 0's allowed). For example, 51 is a 5-7-palindrome because $201_5=51=102_7$. Compute both two-digit 7-10-palindromes. (Express your answer in base 10.)

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-17.prompt: Compute the value of the expression: $$6\sin^2 15^\circ\cos^2 15^\circ+5\cos^4 15^\circ+4\sin^2 15^\circ+\sin^4 15^\circ.$$

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-18.prompt: Archimedes has a machine which outputs integers between 1 and 10, inclusive, so that each integer has a fixed probability (possibly 0) of being produced. The expected value of each output is 7 and the probability that an output is equal to 10 is $p$. Compute the largest possible value of $p$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-19.prompt: Each letter in the word BERNOULLI is written on a scrap of paper (so, there are 9 scraps of paper in use). Four of these scraps are selected at random to make a new "word." Compute the probability that this new word contains exactly one "L".

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-20.prompt: Compute the prime number $p$ such that $16!$ ends in the same number of zeroes when it is written in base 16 as it does when it is written in base $p$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-21.prompt: The sequence $a_1, a_2, a_3,\dots$ is a non-constant arithmetic progression and the terms $a_1, a_2$ and $a_4$ form a geometric progression. Compute the ratio: $\dfrac{a_6}{a_5}$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-22.prompt: If $x=\sqrt[6]{3}$, compute the value of the expression: $(x+1)(x^2+1)(x^2+x+1)(x-1)(x^4-x^2+1)(x^2-x+1)$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-23.prompt: $S$ is a set with 6 elements. Gauss chooses subsets of $S$ with 3 elements so that no two of the chosen subsets have more than 1 element in common. Compute the greatest number of such subsets that Gauss can choose.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-24.prompt: Points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are given in the plane so that $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral with side length 3 and $D$ is equidistant from $A$, $B$ and $C$. Three circles are drawn so that each passes through $D$ and two of $A$, $B$, $C$. Compute the total area enclosed by these circles.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-25.prompt: iTems come in packages of three and five. Cauchy has a coupon so that each package of three iTems costs \$2 while each package of five iTems costs \$4. Compute the smallest amount of money, in dollars, that Cauchy can pay to purchase exactly 35 iTems.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-26.prompt: $ABCDEF$ is a hexagon, all of whose interior angles measure 120 degrees, $AB=CD=3$, $EF=1$ and $BC=6$. Compute $DE$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-27.prompt: If $x$ and $y$ are two positive real numbers such that $6x^2-13xy+5y^2=0$, compute all possible values of $\dfrac{x^2-y^2}{x^2+y^2}$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-28.prompt: Compute the smallest positive integer $n$ such that $25n$ leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 49 and $49n$ leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 25.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-29.prompt: Two sequences are defined recursively by the equations $a_1=3$, $b_1=2$, $a_{n+1}=a_n+b_n$ and $b_{n+1}=a_n-b_n$ for $n\ge1$. Compute $a_{13}$.

nyciml-2007-08-fall-seniora-30.prompt: A rotation in the plane by an angle $\theta$ centered at the point $(a, b)$ maps $(0, 5)$ to $(-8/5, 29/5)$ and maps $(2, -9)$ to $(26/5, -33/5)$. Compute the ordered pair $(a, b)$.
